# Fictional graph-agent corpus v1

This directory contains 22 short fictional records and a deterministic provider-data index. The loopback adapter is `tests/research_graph_archive.py`; its tests do not establish that an agent trial ran. All identities, dates, titles, terminology, numbers and outcomes are invented. No external services, credentials, real people or proprietary source material are needed.

`index.json` defines artifacts and byte hashes, title/body search routes, exact-query result lists, a lexical fallback, pagination, read outcomes and fresh/reuse modes. Documents contain ordinary archive evidence and `[[artifact_id]]` references. They do not give agent-control instructions. A document's genre is source metadata; interpretation belongs to the research worker.

The offline adapter reads the index and documents. **Do not give the index, source directory listing, README or all document files to a worker when measuring discovery.** Give workers only `worker-task.md`, the selected mode's seed responses and the advertised archive route schemas. Retrieve later documents through the adapter. Prefer filesystem isolation when the harness supports it. With agents that share the operator's filesystem, explicitly instruct workers to use only the provider routes and audit their actual tool access. Label that trial as cooperative input withholding, not a sandboxed or adversarial blindness test. Any direct corpus/evaluator read or source hint makes the affected discovery result assisted; preserve its earlier unassisted snapshot separately.

Search uses the exact normalized cases when present and the documented lexical fallback otherwise. Explicit cases model fixed ranked search results; they are not relevance judgments. Apply exclusions before counts, snippets and pagination. Preserve the first result/selection snapshot before direct source hints or corrective interventions. Page size is capped at five so complete versus partial result coverage is observable at low cost.

Run one adapter process per trial. It shares read attempts by trial/artifact/revision across its request threads and persists state across restarts; multiple processes must not share a state file concurrently. One archive read has a transient first failure followed by success; one has a terminal access restriction. A failed read never exposes retained body bytes. Metadata discovery is not substantive inspection. The adapter logs route/query/page/attempt/status; the research recorder retains exact returned bytes and receipts outside this fixture.

Fresh mode supplies only the register and excludes prior-study material from every route. Reuse mode also supplies the prior companion. Keep the arms distinct: using the companion cannot count as independent rediscovery or a new experiment. Both arms use the same underlying primary archive.

The later protocol test should exercise actual child agents, automatic graph ingestion, shared work/budget claims, recoverable interruption and generated views. Structural fixture validation alone proves none of those behaviors. The operator keeps all evaluator relevance/lead/claim judgments outside this repository and out of worker prompts.
